title: Pests in Schools
before:
Order posters and other materials from the Maine CDC

Maine schools are required to adopt integrated pest management (IPM) policies to protect students and staff while promoting academic success. IPM is an environmentally sound approach to managing pests such as insects, weeds, plant pathogens, and wildlife on farms and forests, in our communities, and in our homes. IPM relies on proper pest identification, monitoring, and combinations of pest avoidance and management strategies to protect people, crops, and the environment while minimizing reliance on pesticides.

Visit Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation & Forestry IPM and Maine School IPM for more resources.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — emily.poland@maine.gov → Emily.Poland@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Draw a closing link as the action it is
decisions.why: 1 passage ends with a paragraph holding nothing but a link — the thing the passage was leading up to. Set as running text it looks like any other link in the sentence above it. The site already has one way of drawing an action, so it takes that. The words do not change.

decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
